research_rationale: Executive Order 6321 (October 3, 1933) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362146), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Identity and page check: the page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-09-06T08:31:47Z whose heading names Executive Order 6321, whose date (October 3, 1933) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The census register and the WPA 1944 list (1933 Oct 3, p.542, approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade) give the same date and subject. The reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. No inventory correction was needed: the one machine clause is the operative paragraph, and the opening paragraph only recites the application, hearings and findings.
savings_reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.
earlier_end_check: The order states no period, condition, "until" date or provisional approval of its own. I searched the held order texts (the Cruden lookup and a follow-up search on the code's name and on "Motor Vehicle Retail"), the census register and the WPA 1944 list for later orders that cite EO 6321 by number or name this code. No held order text cites EO 6321 by number. The only held order text that names this code is EO 6948-A (January 18, 1935), which approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Maintenance Trade and refers to the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade: it stays the provisions of the maintenance code for sixty days as to members of the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade insofar as they conflict with the provisions of this code, and directs that the National Industrial Recovery Board, after notice and hearing, determine which provisions of the two codes prevail. That order stays provisions of the maintenance code, not this approval, and no held order text records a determination that modifies or revokes this approval, so it is a later order naming this code and not an end; no source-backed event record for it is available in this packet, so it is not entered in later_events. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.
scope_check: One operative clause (characters 735-1197), the approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade. The order states no condition, exception, stay, exemption or period; its opening paragraph only recites the application, the hearings and the Administrator's findings.

research_rationale: Executive Order 6684-C (April 19, 1934) is an approval of the Electrical Contracting Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry, and a modification of the earlier approval of that code to cover the code as supplemented, under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362453), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). The census register and the WPA 1944 list (1934 Apr 19, p.575, approval of the code for the Electrical Contracting Division of the Construction Industry) give the same date and subject. The order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.

Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.
earlier_end_check: The order states no period, "until" date, condition or provisional approval that limits the approval, and no stay or postponement to a fixed date. The Construction Industry Code was approved January 31, 1934 (EO 6578). A scan of the held 1933-1935 order titles and a text search for "Construction Industry" find, besides EO 6578 and this order, the approvals of sibling chapters and subchapters (EO 6606-D, 6640, 6684-E, 6711-B, 6750-B, 6988-A, 7025-A), EO 6731-A (June 6, 1934), EO 6925-A (December 19, 1934), and many orders of September 1934 to May 1935 approving agreements between members of divisions of the code (EO 6860-A through EO 7036-D by title). I read the operative sentence of EO 6731-A and of each of the seven chapter approvals. Each chapter approval approves a further chapter or subchapter and modifies or amends the parent approval to include the code as supplemented; none cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the Electrical Contracting Chapter or the parent code. EO 6711-B reserves review of, and stays or exemptions from, one section of the plumbing chapter, and EO 6988-A and 7025-A reserve review of a section on mutual agreements with a possible stay of that section; a stay of one section would not end the approval of this chapter. EO 6731-A is a different command: it appoints Sullivan W. Jones as chairman of the National Construction Planning and Adjustment Board during the pleasure of the Administrator, and it does not touch this approval. EO 6925-A cancels the order approving a different code (the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade) and names the Construction Industry Code only as the code that would govern that trade's construction operations after the cancellation. I read the operative sentence of the five held orders approving agreements of the Electrical Contracting Division (EO 6883-B, 6892-A, 6974-A, 6984-A and 7010-F): each approves an agreement and none cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes this chapter. I did not read the other agreement orders; by title they approve agreements among members of code divisions and are separate instruments that this analysis does not decide, and none is titled as a cancellation of the code. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command.
